# ESA: Boundaries of attractors with bounded noise: boundary maps, normal hyperbolicity and singularities Early Stage Assessment report

John Parry

**Status:** drafting

## Abstract

Random dynamical systems with bounded noise have attractors that are compact sets with non-empty interior. Their shape, and in particular the regularity of their boundaries, governs how they change under perturbation. The *boundary map* lifts the set-valued dynamics to a single-valued map on the unit normal bundle $\mathbb{R}^d\times\mathbb{S}^{d-1}$, where it is a conformal contactomorphism. The boundary of the attractor lifts to an invariant Legendrian submanifold. The project studies when this Legendrian submanifold is normally hyperbolic (and hence the boundary is $C^2$-persistent), how normal hyperbolicity is lost, and which singularities (wedges, cusps) appear on the perturbed boundary when it is. This report sets out the problem and background and then analyses the planar diagonal linear case in full. We find the fixed points of the boundary map, their spectra and eigenvectors, and the global heteroclinic structure of the invariant normal bundle. We show that normal hyperbolicity fails under any definition at the resonance $\lambda_1=\lambda_2^2$ (Task 1 of the project), and that with uniform rates it holds if and only if $\lambda_1>\lambda_2^2$. In that case the curvature of $\partial A$ at its flattest points equals $(\lambda_1-\lambda_2^2)/(\varepsilon\lambda_1)$, and it vanishes otherwise. The spectra at fixed points obey a contact pairing rule $\{\rho\}\cup\{\nu,\rho/\nu\}$, and in these terms the resonance is a collision within a conformally symplectic eigenvalue pair. Numerical computations in JAX confirm the results. We close with a plan for the nonlinear resonant perturbation $f(x)=(\lambda^2x_1+ax_2^2,\lambda x_2)$ and its singularities, and with two broader strands: a *linear contact algebra* of boundary maps, and the realisation of boundary maps as *Pontryagin extremal flows* of control systems.
